findings.title: Chunked reader discards chunk terminator without validating CRLF (request smuggling)
findings.evidence:
Reachable sink: after a chunk's payload is fully consumed, ChunkedReader sets self._bytes_to_discard = 2 (h11/_readers.py:197) and on the next __call__ blindly extracts and throws those 2 bytes away via buf.maybe_extract_at_most(self._bytes_to_discard) (h11/_readers.py:164) with no comparison against the required CRLF, then resumes parsing the next chunk header (h11/_readers.py:172-201). Attacker-controlled bytes reach this sink through the normal receive path: Connection.receive_data() -> next_event() selects the SEND_BODY 'chunked' reader (h11/_readers.py:242-244), so any HTTP peer sending 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' drives ChunkedReader directly. Reproduced: feeding a SERVER Connection the body b'5
helloXX5
world
0

' yields Data(b'hello'), Data(b'world'), EndOfMessage() with no error, even though 'XX' is not the RFC 7230 chunk terminator '
'; the reader silently swallows it. Upstream fixed this in h11 0.16.0 by tracking the expected bytes (self._bytes_to_discard = b'
', h11 0.16.0 _readers.py:153/200) and raising LocalProtocolError 'malformed chunk footer' on mismatch (_readers.py:162-174). Because h11 accepts malformed chunk boundaries that strict front-ends/proxies reject (or delimit differently), an attacker can desynchronize where a proxy ends a request body and where h11 resumes parsing, smuggling a second request/response (CVE-2025-43859 / GHSA-vqfr-h8mv-ghfj, CVSS 9.1). The chunk-ext/trailer path is not the root cause; the missing CRLF check on the chunk footer at line 164 is.
